statements.label: supported
statements.text: Testing in human cells yielded 40 integration-competent DNA transposable elements, twice the number of such elements reported in all earlier work combined.
statements.evidence: We identified 40 active (integration-competent) TEs, surpassing the cumulative number (20) of TEs found previously.
statements.note: The abstract gives both counts, 40 newly identified against 20 found previously.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Elements of the Tc1/mariner superfamily were more active than other elements in the comparative dataset.
statements.evidence: we found that the Tc1/mariner superfamily exhibits elevated activity
statements.note: The comparison of activity across superfamilies is one of the reported results.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mariner2_AG inserts into cancer-driver genes less often than the lentiviral vector does.
statements.evidence: Further functional characterization of TEs revealed additional divergence in features such as insertion bias.
statements.note: Insertion bias is said to differ between elements, but no comparison of insertion-site safety between Mariner2_AG and the lentiviral vector is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: For CAR-T therapy against blood and solid tumours, Mariner2_AG worked better than both the lentiviral vector and the transposon vector SB100X.
statements.evidence: Mariner2_AG (MAG), the most active DNA TE identified, largely outperformed two widely used vectors, the lentiviral vector and the TE-based vector SB100X
statements.note: The abstract reports that this element outperformed both named vectors in the CAR-T setting.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Two allosteric aptamers, against CD63 and against EpCAM, formed a combined barcode that selected tumour-specific exosome subtypes.
statements.evidence: The SORTER uses two allosteric aptamers against exosomal marker CD63 and tumor marker EpCAM to create an orthogonal labeling barcode and achieve selective sorting of tumor-specific exosome subtypes.
statements.note: The two aptamer targets and their sorting role are stated directly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: SORTER agreed with biopsy-based grading more closely than serum PSA measurement did in the same patients.
statements.evidence: With a signature of six miRNAs, SORTER differentiated PCa and benign prostatic hyperplasia with an accuracy of 100%.
statements.note: Accuracy figures are given for the assay alone; no comparison against PSA or biopsy grading appears.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Separating metastatic from nonmetastatic prostate cancer was less accurate, at 90.6%, than separating cancer from benign prostatic hyperplasia.
statements.evidence: With a signature of six miRNAs, SORTER differentiated PCa and benign prostatic hyperplasia with an accuracy of 100%. Notably, the diagnostic accuracy reached 90.6% in the classification of metastatic and nonmetastatic PCa.
statements.note: Both accuracies are reported, 100% for the cancer-versus-hyperplasia task and 90.6% for the metastasis task.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A panel of six miRNAs let the assay tell prostate cancer from benign prostatic hyperplasia without error.
statements.evidence: With a signature of six miRNAs, SORTER differentiated PCa and benign prostatic hyperplasia with an accuracy of 100%.
statements.note: The abstract states an accuracy of 100% for this comparison using a six-miRNA signature.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In benchmarks the tool classified viruses better than plasmids, with Matthews correlation coefficients of 95.3% and 77.8% respectively.
statements.evidence: geNomad achieved high classification performance for diverse plasmids and viruses (Matthews correlation coefficient of 77.8% and 95.3%, respectively), substantially outperforming other tools
statements.note: The paired figures are given in that order, 77.8% for plasmids and 95.3% for viruses.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A conditional random field model allows proviruses sitting inside host genomes to be picked out with high precision.
statements.evidence: Using a conditional random field model, geNomad also detects proviruses integrated into host genomes with high precision.
statements.note: The provirus detection approach and its precision are stated as a capability of the framework.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The newly discovered viruses include ones infecting humans that are linked to specific diseases.
statements.evidence: Identifying and characterizing mobile genetic elements in sequencing data is essential for understanding their diversity, ecology, biotechnological applications and impact on public health.
statements.note: Public health relevance is given as motivation; no host assignment or disease link is reported for the viruses found.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Processing more than 2.7 trillion base pairs of sequence data turned up millions of viruses and plasmids, now deposited in IMG/VR and IMG/PR.
statements.evidence: we processed over 2.7 trillion base pairs of sequencing data, leading to the discovery of millions of viruses and plasmids that are available through the IMG/VR and IMG/PR databases
statements.note: The data volume, the scale of the discovery and the two databases are all reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In 24 stage I and II cancer samples, 22.7% of unique reads hit targeted haplotypes with MAPLE against 0.8% with the conventional panel.
statements.evidence: In 24 stage I and II cancer samples, MAPLE maps 22.7% of unique reads to 5045 targeted haplotypes, compared to 0.8% of reads mapping to 190 haplotypes with the conventional method.
statements.note: Both read fractions and both haplotype counts are given for the same 24 early-stage samples.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The MAPLE panel flags colorectal cancer recurrence after surgery earlier than carcinoembryonic antigen monitoring.
statements.evidence: two panels are designed using MAPLE and the conventional method respectively to target 13,264 colorectal cancer (CRC)-related methylation haplotypes and are validated through a blood plasma cohort of 162 samples including CRC patients and controls
statements.note: Validation was a case-control comparison of patients and controls; post-surgical monitoring and CEA are never mentioned.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Reducing input to 0.05% of total sequencing reads cost MAPLE only a modest amount of performance, while the conventional method fell off sharply.
statements.evidence: Even with just 0.05% of total sequencing reads, MAPLE exhibits only a modest performance decline, in contrast to the conventional method's significant decline
statements.note: The down-sampling comparison between the two methods is one of the reported results.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: With a LightGBM classifier the MAPLE panel reached 80% sensitivity at 95% specificity in the plasma cohort.
statements.evidence: Aided by a LightGBM classifier, the MAPLE panel accurately identifies patients with 95% specificity and 80% sensitivity.
statements.note: Both operating figures are stated for the MAPLE panel with that classifier.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Inhibiting PRMT5 in mammalian cells left polyadenylated mRNA and Sm proteins piling up on chromatin.
statements.evidence: PRMT5 inhibition in mammalian cells causes polyadenylated mRNA and Smith antigen (Sm) protein accumulation on chromatin
statements.note: The accumulation of both the transcripts and the Sm proteins on chromatin after inhibition is directly reported.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: PRMT5 inhibitors shrink tumours in mice by trapping transcripts on chromatin.
statements.evidence: We conclude that PRMT5 ensures mRNA processing and nuclear export by preventing aberrant chromatin retention, highlighting arginine methylation as a key regulator of RNA-chromatin dynamics.
statements.note: The work is cell-based and mechanistic; no animal experiments or therapeutic effects are reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The transcripts held on chromatin are rich in introns and are spliced slowly.
statements.evidence: These retained transcripts are intron rich and splice slowly.
statements.note: Both properties of the retained transcripts are stated as findings.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Biochemistry showed the SMN Tudor domain and nucleic acid competing for binding to methylated Sm tails.
statements.evidence: Biochemical assays reveal that the SMN Tudor domain competes with nucleic acid binding of methylated Sm tails.
statements.note: The competition between the Tudor domain and nucleic acid binding comes from the reported biochemical assays.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: SETDB1 expression in mouse skin rose and fell closely in step with stem cell activity.
statements.evidence: dynamic expression of histone methyltransferase SETDB1 (a retrotransposon repressor) closely mirrors stem cell activities in murine skin
statements.note: The abstract reports this correspondence between SETDB1 expression and stem cell activity as an observation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deleting SETDB1 reactivated endogenous retroviruses and produced viral-like particles, causing hair loss and stem cell exhaustion that antiviral drugs reversed.
statements.evidence: SETDB1 ablation leads to the reactivation of endogenous retroviruses (ERVs, a type of retrotransposon) and the assembly of viral-like particles, resulting in hair loss and stem cell exhaustion that is reversible by antiviral drugs.
statements.note: Each part of the chain, from reactivation through the phenotype to its reversal, is stated.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Antiviral drugs restore hair growth in human patients whose alopecia involves retroviral reactivation.
statements.evidence: resulting in hair loss and stem cell exhaustion that is reversible by antiviral drugs
statements.note: The rescue by antiviral drugs is reported in mouse skin, with no human patients studied either way.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: At least two distinct pathways drive the phenotype: antiviral defence in hair follicle stem cells and progenitors, and replication stress in transient amplifying cells.
statements.evidence: at least two molecularly and spatially distinct pathways are responsible: antiviral defense mediated by hair follicle stem cells and progenitors and antiviral-independent response due to replication stress in transient amplifying cells
statements.note: Both pathways and the cell types they act in are named in the abstract.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Running the platform on stool from 20 people produced personalized biobanks of 26,997 isolates, covering over 80% of the abundant taxa present.
statements.evidence: Application of this platform on fecal samples from 20 humans yields personalized gut microbiome biobanks totaling 26,997 isolates that represented >80% of all abundant taxa.
statements.note: The donor count, isolate count and taxon coverage are all given in one sentence.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Isolates picked by the robotic platform stayed viable after a year of frozen storage.
statements.evidence: Here we describe an open-source high-throughput robotic strain isolation platform for the rapid generation of isolates on demand.
statements.note: The platform generates isolates on demand, but nothing is reported about how long stored isolates survive.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Spatial analysis of more than 100,000 imaged colonies showed cogrowth between the Ruminococcaceae, Bacteroidaceae, Coriobacteriaceae and Bifidobacteriaceae families.
statements.evidence: Spatial analysis on >100,000 visually captured colonies reveals cogrowth patterns between Ruminococcaceae, Bacteroidaceae, Coriobacteriaceae and Bifidobacteriaceae families
statements.note: The number of colonies and the four families showing cogrowth are reported directly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Comparing 1,197 high-quality genomes from the biobanks revealed strain evolution, selection and horizontal gene transfer both within and between individuals.
statements.evidence: Comparative analysis of 1,197 high-quality genomes from these biobanks shows interesting intra- and interpersonal strain evolution, selection and horizontal gene transfer.
statements.note: The genome count and the three processes seen within and between people are stated.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Long-read sequencing of four karyotypically different Papaver species gave nearly complete assemblies covering 45 centromeres without gaps.
statements.evidence: we used long-read sequencing to generate nearly complete genome assemblies for four karyotypically diverse Papaver species, P. setigerum (2n = 44), P. somniferum (2n = 22), P. rhoeas (2n = 14), and P. bracteatum (2n = 14), collectively representing 45 gapless centromeres
statements.note: The four species and the total of 45 gapless centromeres are both reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Four families of centromere satellite were identified, and two representatives of them were validated experimentally.
statements.evidence: We identified four centromere satellite (cenSat) families and experimentally validated two representatives.
statements.note: The number of families and the experimental validation of two are stated.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Comparing peri-centromeric regions between the species uncovered extensive chromosome rearrangements mediated by centromeres.
statements.evidence: An interspecies comparison of the peri-centromeric regions further revealed extensive centromere-mediated chromosome rearrangements.
statements.note: This rearrangement finding comes from the reported interspecies comparison of peri-centromeric regions.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The Papaver centromere satellite families resemble centromere satellites of other plant genera in sequence.
statements.evidence: We identified four centromere satellite (cenSat) families and experimentally validated two representatives.
statements.note: The satellite families are described within Papaver only; no comparison with satellites outside the genus is made.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: TnpBmax causes fewer off-target edits than Cas9 at matched on-target efficiency.
statements.evidence: We further generated an extensive dataset on TnpBmax editing efficiencies at 10,211 target sites. This enabled us to delineate rules for on-target and off-target editing
statements.note: Off-target rules were derived for TnpBmax itself; no head-to-head comparison with Cas9 is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Redesigning ISDra2 TnpB for mammalian cells raised editing by an average of 4.4-fold.
statements.evidence: we optimized the design of Deinococcus radiodurans (ISDra2) TnpB for application in mammalian cells (TnpBmax), leading to an average 4.4-fold improvement in editing
statements.note: The average fold improvement for the optimized design is stated.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The deep learning predictor TEEP forecasts ISDra2 TnpB guiding RNA activity with a correlation coefficient above 0.8.
statements.evidence: capable of predicting ISDra2 TnpB guiding RNA (ωRNA) activity with high performance (r > 0.8)
statements.note: The abstract gives the model's predictive performance as r > 0.8.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: After AAV delivery, editing reached 75.3% in mouse liver, higher than the 65.9% measured in mouse brain.
statements.evidence: Employing TEEP, we achieved editing efficiencies up to 75.3% in the murine liver and 65.9% in the murine brain after adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector delivery of TnpBmax.
statements.note: Both tissue efficiencies are given, with the liver value above the brain value.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cryo-electron microscopy captured two vertebrate A-clade R2 proteins at the start of target-primed reverse transcription and again after cDNA synthesis and second-strand nicking.
statements.evidence: we report high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy structures of two vertebrate A-clade R2 proteins at the initiation of target-primed reverse transcription and after cDNA synthesis and second-strand nicking
statements.note: The two captured states of the two proteins are described directly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Each of the three zinc-finger domains has its own distinct role in recognizing nucleic acid.
statements.evidence: we illuminate the basis for high selectivity of template use and unique roles for each of the three zinc-finger domains in nucleic acid recognition
statements.note: The distinct roles of all three zinc fingers come from the reported biochemical and cellular assays.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: A-clade R2 proteins insert transgenes into ribosomal DNA more precisely than CRISPR-based knock-in methods do.
statements.evidence: Recently, we demonstrated that avian A-clade R2 proteins achieve efficient and precise insertion of transgenes into their native safe-harbor loci in human cells.
statements.note: Precise insertion is reported for R2 proteins alone, with no comparison against CRISPR-based approaches.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: An unexpected insertion motif found only in vertebrate A-clade R2 proteins reinforces the architecture of the reverse transcriptase active site.
statements.evidence: Reverse transcriptase active site architecture is reinforced by an unanticipated insertion motif specific to vertebrate A-clade R2 proteins.
statements.note: The motif, its restriction to vertebrate A-clade proteins and its structural role are all stated.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients whose tumours over-splice bona-fide 3' UTR introns have shorter overall survival.
statements.evidence: Bona-fide 3UI-transcripts are over-spliced in cancer samples.
statements.note: Over-splicing in tumour samples is reported, but no survival or other clinical outcome is analysed.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: UPF1 expression ran inversely to 3UI-splicing in normal samples, a relationship absent in colon cancer samples.
statements.evidence: Expression of NMD component UPF1 negatively correlates with 3UI-splicing in normal, but not colon cancer, samples.
statements.note: The negative correlation and its absence in colon cancer are both reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The transcriptome assembly drew on 7897 solid tumour and normal samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas and yielded thousands of 3UI-containing transcripts.
statements.evidence: We present a transcriptome assembly built from 7897 solid tumour and normal samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas. We identify thousands of 3UI-containing transcripts, many expressed across multiple cancer types.
statements.note: The sample count and the number of transcripts recovered are given together.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among the differentially spliced 3UI transcripts enriched in Wnt signalling in colon cancer, CTNNB1 showed the largest increase in splicing.
statements.evidence: In colon cancer, differentially-spliced 3UI transcripts are enriched in the Wnt signalling pathway, with CTNNB1 showing the greatest increase in splicing.
statements.note: The pathway enrichment and CTNNB1 as the biggest riser are both stated.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Spacers acquired on solid medium protect cells against phage infection better than spacers acquired in liquid culture.
statements.evidence: The assay provides a scalable platform for dissecting condition-specific features of CRISPR-Cas adaptation, including spacer origin, sequence features, and growth context.
statements.note: The work measures spacer acquisition and its sources; no phage challenge or interference experiment is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Plasmid-derived spacers made up 64% of those acquired in liquid culture but only about 9% on solid medium.
statements.evidence: in liquid culture, 64% of spacers were plasmid-derived, but on solid medium this dropped to ∼9%
statements.note: Both percentages are reported for the shift in spacer source bias between growth conditions.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Spacer acquisition repairs the reading frame of a broken lacZ gene, so individual events show up as blue papillae on lactose X-gal plates.
statements.evidence: Spacer acquisition restores the reading frame of a disrupted lacZ gene, forming blue papillae on lactose X-gal plates.
statements.note: The readout mechanism of the assay is described in exactly these terms.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Matching the inducer concentration to liquid-culture conditions did not bring the plasmid bias back on solid medium.
statements.evidence: Adjusting inducer concentration to match liquid conditions did not restore plasmid bias, indicating a physiological basis linked to colony growth.
statements.note: The failure of the inducer adjustment to restore the bias is a reported result.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: METTL3 places m6A marks on TP53 mRNA itself, raising how much p53 protein is translated.
statements.evidence: Together, these studies reveal a fundamental role for METTL3 in amplifying p53 signaling in response to cellular stress.
statements.note: The abstract names catalytic and non-catalytic mechanisms in general but never says which transcripts METTL3 methylates.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tandem affinity purification with mass spectrometry picked out METTL3, a constituent of the m6A methyltransferase complex, as a p53 interactor.
statements.evidence: This approach identified METTL3, an m 6 A RNA-methyltransferase complex (MTC) constituent, as a p53 interactor.
statements.note: The interaction screen and its hit are reported in the abstract.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: METTL3 stabilizes p53 protein and boosts its target gene expression after DNA damage and oncogenic signals, through both catalytic and non-catalytic mechanisms.
statements.evidence: We find that METTL3 promotes p53 protein stabilization and target gene expression in response to DNA damage and oncogenic signals, by both catalytic activity-dependent and independent mechanisms.
statements.note: Both effects and both classes of mechanism are stated as findings.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The tumour-suppressive effect of METTL3 appeared only when p53 was intact.
statements.evidence: Notably, METTL3 only promotes tumor suppression in the context of intact p53.
statements.note: The dependence of the effect on intact p53 is reported directly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of 605 CRE isolates genotyped by Illumina sequencing, 435 carried blaKPC and were then nanopore sequenced for hybrid assembly.
statements.evidence: Six hundred and five CRE isolates collected between 2009 and 2018 first underwent Illumina sequencing for genome-wide genotyping; 435 bla KPC -positive isolates were then successfully nanopore sequenced
statements.note: Both isolate counts and the two sequencing steps are reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Clonal transmission was evident in 66% of isolates, while plasmid-mediated blaKPC acquisition accounted for 23% to 27%.
statements.evidence: We found evidence for clonal transmission in 66% of CRE isolates, over half of which belonged to four clades comprising K. pneumoniae ST258. Plasmid-mediated acquisition of bla KPC occurred in 23%-27% of isolates.
statements.note: Both routes are quantified, 66% clonal against 23-27% plasmid-mediated.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The isolates spanned 96 multilocus sequence types and carried blaKPC on 447 plasmids, which grouped into 54 clusters.
statements.evidence: Overall, CRE isolates belonged to 96 multilocus sequence types (STs) encoding bla KPC on 447 plasmids which formed 54 plasmid clusters.
statements.note: All three counts are given in a single reported sentence.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients infected with strains that acquired blaKPC by plasmid had worse clinical outcomes than those with clonally transmitted strains.
statements.evidence: Plasmid-mediated acquisition of bla KPC occurred in 23%-27% of isolates.
statements.note: The study characterizes transmission routes among isolates; no patient outcome data are reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Reference Sample A yielded over 40,000 variants down to 1% allele frequency, more than 25,000 of them below 20%, with 1653 in COSMIC-related genes.
statements.evidence: In reference Sample A, we identify more than 40,000 variants down to 1% allele frequency with more than 25,000 variants having less than 20% allele frequency with 1653 variants in COSMIC-related genes.
statements.note: All three variant counts are reported for Sample A.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.evidence: to develop a reference sample with suitably large numbers of coding positions with known (variant) positives and negatives for properly evaluating oncopanel analytical performance
statements.note: The characterization described covers coding variant positions; structural and copy number content is neither claimed nor excluded.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: More than 300 randomly chosen loci were checked independently by droplet digital PCR and agreed completely with the sequencing calls.
statements.evidence: Over 300 loci are randomly selected and independently verified via droplet digital PCR with 100% concordance.
statements.note: The orthogonal verification and its 100% concordance are reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mixing Sample A with normal Sample B produces samples holding known variants at allele frequencies as low as 0.02%, a range fit for liquid biopsy panels.
statements.evidence: including known variants having allele frequency of 0.02%, a range suitable for assessing liquid biopsy panels
statements.note: The admixture strategy and the 0.02% allele frequency it reaches are both stated.
